trade_setups.thesis: Energy is the only clear beneficiary of the Iran/oil shock. WTI +9.42% to $78.14 while XLE sits at $55.08 represents lagged sector catch-up. High-oil, rising-yield regime inflects energy FCF strongly; geopolitical premium may prove stickier than consensus.

Tech ETF -1.53% to $182.93 today. Elevated yields + oil inflation = worst macro regime for high-multiple growth. Iran semiconductor export risk adds sector-specific pressure. CPI risk asymmetrically bad for tech.
AMD -4%, MU -4%, SK Hynix -9%; semis led today's downside with specific chip-supply narrative. If CPI hot Tuesday, the May 15 SOXX short setup repeats. Conditional — do not enter before CPI.

bear_case: Counter-argument: Iran oil spikes historically mean-revert within 48-72 hours once diplomatic channels open or markets recognize the Strait of Hormuz disruption is a tariff, not supply destruction. The 30Y at 5.101% is +3bps from Friday, not the +12bps shock of May 15. June CPI will capture a month when WTI fell -20.4%, likely printing below consensus; a cool number Tuesday could trigger a violent intraday reversal. Banks reporting strong Q2 NII and resilient credit would replicate the May 20 BUY upgrade dynamic where the Step Aside resolved in three sessions. VIX at 16.89 has not confirmed regime break. Invalidation level: if SPX reclaims 7,600 by Wednesday with VIX below 17 and 30Y retreating below 4.90%, the Iran shock was a one-day overshoot and the call is wrong.
